about: The epistola of the formulary “Christ the King” in the 1962 Roman Missal.

seg.tr: Brethren: We give thanks to God the Father, who made us worthy of a share in the lot of the saints in the light, who delivered us from the dominion of darkness and carried us over into the kingdom of the Son of His love, in whom we have redemption through His blood, the remission of sins, who is the image of the invisible God, firstborn of every creature, for in Him were made all things in the heavens and on earth, the visible and the invisible, whether thrones or dominions or principalities or powers; through Him and in Him all things have been created, and He Himself is before all, and all things subsist in Him. And He is the head of the body, the Church, being the beginning, firstborn from the dead, that in all things He Himself may hold the first place; because it was well pleasing that all fullness should dwell in Him, and by Him to reconcile all things to Him, making peace through the blood of His cross, whether the things on earth or the things in the heavens, in Christ Jesus our Lord.

ex.w108: The subject of complácuit is not expressed. Omnem plenitúdinem is accusative, the subject of the infinitive inhabitáre, so “all fullness” is not the one who is pleased. The opening of the reading (Deo Patri … qui erípuit nos … et tránstulit) and the masculine participle pacíficans point to God the Father.
ex.w119: The participle describes God’s peacemaking through the blood of Christ’s cross. Its subject is understood, not expressed by a separate noun here.
